title: Finite principal-localization data of a locally homogeneous twist section
statement: Let A be an N-graded commutative ring with grading 𝒜, k an integer, f homogeneous of positive degree b, and s a section of twist 𝒜 k [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] on D₊(f). Set B=A_(f) and M=A_f, viewed as a B-module by the canonical homogeneous-localization inclusion. There exist a finite family g_i in B spanning the unit ideal and elements t_i in M localized at g_i, compatible on every overlap under the canonical module localization maps [lem-weil-pbc-cover-module-exact]. At each homogeneous prime p in D₊(f), there is an index i and an additive evaluation map from M localized at g_i to A_p sending every z/1 to the canonical image of z in A_p and sending t_i to the value s(p). This is only compatible local data; the statement does not assert a global element of M.

source.place: Lemma 27.8.4 and its preceding construction, specialized to the shift A(k); this split separates ordinary gluing from degree detection

proof.text:
at each point use the local homogeneous-fraction witness of s. Choose a
homogeneous basic neighborhood inside its witness neighborhood and D₊(f). Multiply the
witness denominator by this neighborhood's defining element and by f, and multiply the
numerator by the same factors. The resulting homogeneous denominator h has positive
degree c and D₊(h) lies in the witness neighborhood. For u = h^b/f^c in A_(f), the affine
chart identifies D₊(h) inside D₊(f) with D(u). Quasi-compactness gives finitely many such
neighborhoods. Their chart elements u_i generate the unit ideal. In A_f localized at u_i,
h_i is invertible since h_i^b = u_i*f^c_i and f is invertible, so the witness fraction
defines t_i. On an overlap use the homogeneous element f*h_i*h_j of A. Both fractions
have the same evaluations s(p) at every point of its basic open, so homogeneous-prime
equality detection makes them equal in A localized at f*h_i*h_j. The universal properties
identify this ring localization with the iterated module localization at u_i*u_j, giving
the displayed compatibility. At a point of D(u_i), u_i maps to a unit in A_p; the ordinary
evaluation A_f → A_p therefore extends to the further localization. Its underlying
additive map sends z/1 to the ordinary evaluation of z and t_i to s(p). Every point lies
in some neighborhood. If the open is empty, f is nilpotent and both A_f and A_(f) are
zero; the empty cover has span top in this zero ring and evaluation is vacuous.

proof_origin.place: Finite basic-open refinement and local fractions from the construction preceding Definition 27.8.3; overlap equality via homogeneous-prime localization detection

lean.statement: theorem twist_finiteLocalization_data {A σ : Type v} [CommRing A] [SetLike σ A] [AddSubgroupClass σ A] (𝒜 : ℕ → σ) [GradedRing 𝒜] (k : ℤ) (f : A) (b : ℕ) (hb : 0 < b) (hf : f ∈ 𝒜 b) (s : (twist 𝒜 k).val.obj (op (basicOpen 𝒜 f))) : let B := HomogeneousLocalization.Away 𝒜 f let M := LocalizedModule.Away f A letI : Module B M := Module.compHom M (algebraMap B (Localization.Away f)) ∃ (n : ℕ) (g : Fin n → B) (hspan : Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤), let ρ := fun (a h : B) (ha : a ∣ h) ↦ IsLocalizedModule.lift (Submonoid.powers a) (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers a) M) (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers h) M) (RingTheory.localizationAway_map_units_of_dvd (M := M) a h ha) ∃ t : ∀ i : Fin n, LocalizedModule.Away (g i) M, (∀ i j : Fin n, ρ (g i) (g i * g j) (dvd_mul_right (g i) (g j)) (t i) = ρ (g j) (g i * g j) (dvd_mul_left (g j) (g i)) (t j)) ∧ ∀ p : basicOpen 𝒜 f, ∃ (i : Fin n) (e : LocalizedModule.Away (g i) M →+ Localization.AtPrime p.1.asHomogeneousIdeal.toIdeal), (∀ z : M, e (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers (g i)) M z) = IsLocalization.map (M := Submonoid.powers f) (T := p.1.asHomogeneousIdeal.toIdeal.primeCompl) (Localization.AtPrime p.1.asHomogeneousIdeal.toIdeal) (RingHom.id A) (Submonoid.powers_le.mpr p.2) z) ∧ e (t i) = (s.1 p).1
